title: Testing one-to-one periodicity

problem.name: Testing one-to-one periodicity
problem.statement_latex: Given $f:[n]\to[n]$, distinguish functions whose values repeat injectively with a period in $[\sqrt n/4,\sqrt n/2]$ from functions $\varepsilon$-far from every such periodic function. Complexity counts value queries.
problem.statement_text: Given $f:[n]\to[n]$, distinguish functions whose values repeat injectively with a period in $[\sqrt n/4,\sqrt n/2]$ from functions $\varepsilon$-far from every such periodic function. Complexity counts value queries.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.
evidence.description_text: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.
hardware.description_text: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $O_\varepsilon(1)$ oracle queries and $\operatorname{poly}(\log n)$ additional processing by Chakraborty--Fischer--Matsliah--de Wolf, using Fourier period testing.
quantum.headline_text: $O_\varepsilon(1)$ oracle queries and $\operatorname{poly}(\log n)$ additional processing by Chakraborty–Fischer–Matsliah–de Wolf, using Fourier period testing.

classical.headline_latex: $\Omega(n^{1/4}/\log n)$ randomized queries are necessary; a classical tester can use collisions to infer candidate periods and verify them.
